sourcedFrom: Safety & Instruction Manual Omega Muzzleloading Rifle — REV:OMEGAML_04-30-2012, P/N 00084007 (2012)
cleanIntro: The Omega is a swinging-breech-block inline: the trigger guard pivots forward to drop the breech block, and it is ignited by a 209 primer seated in a pocket in the breech plug. Every step below is Thompson/Center's own Omega procedure. The Northwest Explorer looks like this rifle and is not this rifle — it takes a Number 11 cap on a nipple, so none of its priming wording belongs here.

steps.title: Confirm the rifle is unprimed and uncharged
steps.action: Nothing else starts until this is settled. A muzzleloader will not show you an empty chamber, so the verification is the procedure below, not a glance.
steps.caution: Never attempt to clean a charged or primed muzzleloading firearm.
steps.quote: Make sure that the gun is unprimed and uncharged.
steps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual Omega Muzzleloading Rifle — REV:OMEGAML_04-30-2012, P/N 00084007 — Takedown of the Omega Muzzleloader — p.37

steps.title: Pivot the trigger guard forward to drop the breech block
steps.action: This is the Omega's own opening motion. The trigger guard is the lever; swinging it forward lowers the breech block and brings the primer pocket into view.
steps.quote: Lower the swinging breech block to open the action by pivoting the trigger guard forward. This will expose the primer pocket in the breech plug.
steps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual Omega Muzzleloading Rifle — REV:OMEGAML_04-30-2012, P/N 00084007 — Takedown of the Omega Muzzleloader — p.37

steps.title: Check the pocket, then sight the ignition fire channel
steps.action: With the pocket exposed, confirm no primer is seated. Then hold the muzzle up to a light and look down the ignition fire channel from the breech end — daylight through it is what proves the barrel is empty.
steps.quote: Make sure there is no primer seated. Next, holding the muzzle up to the light, look through the ignition fire channel to make sure you can see through it.
steps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual Omega Muzzleloading Rifle — REV:OMEGAML_04-30-2012, P/N 00084007 — Takedown of the Omega Muzzleloader — p.37
steps.warn: If you cannot see through it, the rifle is charged or the channel is obstructed. Stop and unload.

steps.title: If it is charged, take the plug out and let gravity unload it
steps.action: With the rifle confirmed unprimed, remove the breech plug and stand the muzzle up. Powder comes out of the breech first; the projectile is pushed clear afterwards with the ramrod and its extension.
steps.quote: Once the breech plug has been removed, point the muzzle up. Gravity should then cause the pellets or the loose powder to drop out.
steps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual Omega Muzzleloading Rifle — REV:OMEGAML_04-30-2012, P/N 00084007 — Unloading a Charge from the Omega Muzzleloader — p.30

steps.title: Remove the ramrod
steps.action: Slide the ramrod out of the thimbles under the barrel and set it aside — you want it free before the barreled action comes out of the stock.
steps.quote: Remove the ramrod from the thimble(s).
steps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual Omega Muzzleloading Rifle — REV:OMEGAML_04-30-2012, P/N 00084007 — Takedown of the Omega Muzzleloader — p.37

steps.title: Close the breech and back out both stock screws
steps.action: Close the swinging breech first so nothing is under tension, then take out the two stock/lug assembly screws — one about an inch ahead of the trigger guard, the other about four inches ahead of that.
steps.quote: Close the swinging breech and remove both the front and rear stock/lug assembly screws by turning them counter clockwise.
steps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual Omega Muzzleloading Rifle — REV:OMEGAML_04-30-2012, P/N 00084007 — Takedown of the Omega Muzzleloader — p.37

steps.title: Lift the barrel and action out of the stock
steps.action: With both screws out the barreled action comes straight up out of the stock. That is the Omega in its two basic groups: the barrel and action assembly, and the stock.
steps.quote: The barrel/action assembly may now be lifted out of the stock.
steps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual Omega Muzzleloading Rifle — REV:OMEGAML_04-30-2012, P/N 00084007 — Takedown of the Omega Muzzleloader — p.37

steps.title: Unscrew the breech plug
steps.action: Open the breech, fit the wrench, and turn counter-clockwise. It will resist at first — that is the gas seal from the last time it was snugged, and it has to be broken. If the barrel turns in your hand, hold the barrel lug in a vise or a crescent wrench for leverage.
steps.aside: The Omega's plug is a conventional threaded plug — it is not the quarter-turn Speed Breech used on the Triumph, and the two procedures are not interchangeable.
steps.quote: Open the breech, and insert the breech plug wrench onto the breech plug. Turn counter clockwise to unscrew the breech plug.
steps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual Omega Muzzleloading Rifle — REV:OMEGAML_04-30-2012, P/N 00084007 — Takedown of the Omega Muzzleloader — p.37

steps.title: Run the bore with the supplied jag
steps.action: Thread the jag onto the ramrod, soak a patch in black-powder solvent, and work it up and down the bore until the fouling stops coming out. Follow with dry patches until the bore is dry.
steps.prose: Black-powder residue is corrosive rather than merely dirty — it will pit a bore that is left overnight.
steps.quote: Use the cleaning jag that was provided with the Omega, and a cleaning patch saturated with a bore cleaner like Thompson/Center’s Number 13® Bore Cleaner or T-17® Bore Cleaner.
steps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual Omega Muzzleloading Rifle — REV:OMEGAML_04-30-2012, P/N 00084007 — Field Cleaning — p.33

steps.title: Clean and oil the breech assembly and firing pin
steps.action: Soft bristle brush with bore cleaner over the breech assembly, dry it, then a light oil. Finish with moisture-displacing oil into the firing pin inside the breech block.
steps.quote: Clean the breech assembly with a soft bristle brush dampened with some bore cleaner. When the breech assembly is dry, lightly oil it.
steps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual Omega Muzzleloading Rifle — REV:OMEGAML_04-30-2012, P/N 00084007 — Field Cleaning — p.33

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: The barrel is clear, the barreled action is out of the stock, the plug is out and the bore and breech are serviced. That is routine maintenance on the Omega. The manual's own thorough-cleaning and full takedown detail is in the Deep Clean.
steps.quote: If the Omega muzzleloader has become very dirty due to extensive firing, the shooter may want to disassemble the rifle further than just removing the breech plug.
steps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual Omega Muzzleloading Rifle — REV:OMEGAML_04-30-2012, P/N 00084007 — Thorough Cleaning — p.36

deepSteps.title: Scrub the plug, then the barrel's own threads
deepSteps.action: Fouling collects in both thread sets and anti-seize is what keeps the plug from welding itself in over a season. Do the plug and the barrel's internal breech threads as two separate jobs.
deepSteps.quote: Once removed, the breech plug should be scrubbed free of fouling and should then be lubricated with an anti-seize lubricant like T/C's Super Lube, before reinstallation.
deepSteps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual Omega Muzzleloading Rifle — REV:OMEGAML_04-30-2012, P/N 00084007 — Thorough Cleaning — p.35

deepSteps.title: Flush the barrel with hot soapy water
deepSteps.action: Stand the muzzle in a pan of hot soapy water and pump a wet patch on the jag from the breech end. The barrel draws water through itself and carries the fouling out.
deepSteps.caution: Dry the bore completely before oiling it. Water left in a black-powder barrel rusts it quickly.
deepSteps.quote: Pump the ramrod and patch up and down in the barrel. This will draw water into the barrel and flush out the fouling.
deepSteps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual Omega Muzzleloading Rifle — REV:OMEGAML_04-30-2012, P/N 00084007 — Thorough Cleaning — p.35

deepSteps.title: Wipe the frame assembly down and dry it
deepSteps.action: Powder residue works its way into the frame every time the breech is opened. Wipe it all out, dry it, and put a light film of oil on — light, because heavy oil congeals in the cold and slows the hammer.
deepSteps.quote: Thoroughly wipe any powder residue from the frame assembly. Dry the parts thoroughly and lubricate them lightly to prevent rust and corrosion.
deepSteps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual Omega Muzzleloading Rifle — REV:OMEGAML_04-30-2012, P/N 00084007 — Thorough Cleaning — p.35

deepSteps.title: Anti-seize the barrel's breech threads before the plug goes back
deepSteps.action: This is the step that decides whether the plug comes out easily next time. Get anti-seize onto the threads inside the barrel, not just onto the plug.
deepSteps.quote: Lubricate the threads inside the breech area of the barrel with anti-seize lubricant.
deepSteps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual Omega Muzzleloading Rifle — REV:OMEGAML_04-30-2012, P/N 00084007 — Thorough Cleaning — p.36

deepSteps.title: Seat the plug to snug — T/C defines it by feel
deepSteps.action: Turn the plug in clockwise with the wrench, carefully, feeling that the threads have started straight. There is no torque figure; the manual gives you a hand test instead, and it is a usable one.
deepSteps.caution: Be certain the threads are not cross-threaded before applying force.
deepSteps.quote: “Snug” is defined as being as tight as you can turn it into the barrel by using the breech plug wrench and turning it clockwise, while holding the barrel in your hand.
deepSteps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual Omega Muzzleloading Rifle — REV:OMEGAML_04-30-2012, P/N 00084007 — Disassembly of the Omega — p.38

deepSteps.title: Reassemble in reverse and function-check before loading
deepSteps.action: Everything goes back the way it came apart, and the rifle does not see a charge again until the trigger and hammer have been checked working.
deepSteps.quote: To reassemble, reverse these steps, making sure that you check for proper functioning of the trigger/hammer mechanism prior to loading and firing.
deepSteps.cite: Safety & Instruction Manual Omega Muzzleloading Rifle — REV:OMEGAML_04-30-2012, P/N 00084007 — Disassembly of the Omega — p.38

cleaning.name: Bore
tasks: Solvent-soaked patches on the supplied jag, up and down until they come out clean
Dry patches until the bore is dry
Lightly lubricate the bore once it is completely dry

cleaning.name: Breech and frame
tasks: Soft bristle brush with bore cleaner over the breech assembly, then dry and lightly oil
Moisture-displacing oil into the firing pin within the breech block
Wipe all powder residue out of the frame assembly and dry it

cleaning.name: Breech plug
tasks: Scrub the plug free of fouling
Clean the barrel's internal breech threads with a stiff brush and bore cleaner, then dry
Anti-seize both the plug threads and the barrel threads

reassembly: Anti-seize the plug threads and the barrel's breech threads
Thread the breech plug in clockwise with the wrench until snug, checking it is not cross-threaded
Lower the barreled action back into the stock
Fit and tighten both stock/lug assembly screws
Return the ramrod to the thimbles
fncheck: With the rifle unprimed and uncharged, work the trigger guard through its full swing and check the hammer and trigger mechanism for proper function before loading and firing — the manual requires this check after any disassembly.
